transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's get started. We've got the talent-show finale going live this Saturday at 9:00 PM Eastern, and we need to finalize the voting package tonight so it can be documented before transmission. The current draft has viewers voting by SMS or through an online portal, open to our broadcast audience. Before I make the final binding decision on the voting package, I want to hear from each of you — standards, platform production, rights, and data protection. What issues or concerns do we need to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a standards issue. The network's current standards memo, which I issued after the draft voting rules were circulated, specifies three requirements that the current draft doesn't yet reflect: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. These need to be incorporated into the final voting package before transmission.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the results of the platform certification test I completed this morning. The SMS integration failed certification, so SMS voting cannot be used as things stand. The web portal did pass certification, but the approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means the final voting package needs to drop SMS as a voting method and account verification must be built into the portal voting flow.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today, and it confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may not use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so those need to be removed before the final voting package is approved.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue. My privacy review, completed with the voting vendor this week, limits participation to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada, and requires voter identifiers to be deleted within 30 days. The current draft still describes worldwide participation and has no deletion step. Both of these need to be corrected in the final voting package before transmission.
